snippet.title: Our House Was On Fire. I Didn't Even Know
snippet.description:
Our house was on fire. I didn't even know.
Last weekend I was heading out on a dirt bike ride with Jack and the Sweet Loaf. I forgot something in my bedroom and ran back inside. That's when I smelled smoke.
Around the corner of the house a fence post was actively burning. The mulch had been smoldering underground for nearly 24 hours — building heat completely undetected beneath the surface. If I hadn't forgotten something in my room we would have come home to a smoking crater.
That was the wake-up call.
We are four weeks ahead of normal fire season this year due to drought and low snowfall. So today I'm going through our complete urban interface fire kit — everything I keep on hand to protect this property, my neighbors, and anyone who needs help moving fast on a fire before it becomes a conflagration.
This kit is built around a traditional US Forest Service fire cache. Two men can throw it in the back of a truck and equip three to four people immediately. Chainsaw, hand tools, drip torch, trauma kit, paper maps, water bladder — everything in one place ready to go.
If you live in the urban interface, wildland urban interface, or anywhere fire prone — save this video. These are the things you want in place before you need them. Not after.
May God bless you and your families.
— Cody

snippet.title: It Doesn’t End When the War Stops
snippet.description:
Most people think this ends when the headlines calm down. It doesn’t.

The pressure is already spreading—from oil into food and even medications. And this is how real shortages begin… upstream, before most people notice.

By the time it’s obvious, prices have already moved and options get tighter.

In my latest video, I break down what’s coming next—and what I’m doing right now to prepare before it hits harder at the household level.
